title: A general-purpose, high-fidelity interface for touch and physical force

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a hand interface that lets people manipulate digital or remote objects while reliably feeling their shape, resistance, texture, slip, and motion. It would coordinate tactile feedback—the sensations produced at the skin—with kinesthetic feedback, such as resistance to finger movement. These complementary capabilities would need to work together across multiple fingers and both hands while preserving comfortable movement. This describes the intended capability, not an achievement established by the supplied evidence.

Scope definition: general purpose means useful across varied objects, materials, and manipulation tasks rather than a single programmed sensation or force-control exercise. High fidelity means that the feedback conveys relevant physical properties consistently enough to guide action, with forces delivered at the appropriate location and in the appropriate direction. The intended interface would avoid dependence on a bulky stationary machine. Thermal sensation and pain are optional extensions, not requirements for this concept.

significance.text: If achieved, this capability would make physical properties available as a much richer medium for computer interaction. People could adjust a grip when an object begins to slip, feel how a simulated material yields, or regulate contact with a remote object using information supplied through their hands. The N2D study provides a limited technical basis for this reasoning: directional force feedback improved some measures of force regulation and user experience in a teleoperation experiment. Extending those benefits to diverse objects and sensations remains conditional on the proposed breakthrough.

Conditional impact synthesis: richer simulation and force-informed remote manipulation would follow directly from reliable physical feedback. Training, design, and collaborative manipulation could become more closely connected to the physical skills people already use. Remote surgery, manufacturing, and repair would require additional advances and validation in robots, sensing, communications, and application-specific safety. A convincing sensation at the hand would not by itself establish that a remote system can measure, reproduce, or safely act on the corresponding physical interaction.

Interpretive limit: describing physical interaction as a general computational medium is an analogy about an expanded interface capability. It does not imply that arbitrary digital objects could acquire every property of real matter, that simulated practice would always transfer to physical work, or that the interface would replace physical objects. The revolutionary judgment rests on the proposed combination of breadth, perceptual fidelity, and freedom of movement; a useful improvement in one force-feedback task establishes a narrower result.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central unsolved capability is coordinated tactile and directional force feedback across the hand without unacceptable restrictions on movement, fit, or endurance. The supplied paper grounds this integration challenge by discussing complementary haptic capabilities and by identifying gaps among the systems its authors reviewed. That comparison supports the research goal but does not establish that every contemporary system has the same limitations or that these are the only barriers.

Concrete engineering barriers include extending directional coverage, coordinating feedback across multiple digits, accommodating individual hand geometry through fitting and calibration, and reducing wearable mass while retaining useful force delivery. N2D illustrates these tradeoffs: its three-finger design provides planar feedback, leaves the direction associated with finger adduction and abduction unreflected, requires user-specific calibration, and can become fatiguing during extended use. These are documented limitations of that device, not universal limits on haptic engineering.

Research-goal synthesis: a general interface would also need to coordinate changing contact locations and force directions so that shape, texture, slip, and compliance remain mutually consistent during manipulation. Increasing actuator coverage alone would not establish this perceptual result. The scientific and engineering challenge includes determining which combinations of cues support reliable perception and action across users and tasks, then delivering those cues with sustained comfort and safe behavior.

Alternative-route synthesis: direct nervous-system stimulation could be another route to artificial touch, but the supplied evidence does not establish its mechanisms, maturity, or remaining technical barriers. It is not a necessary component of HCI-03. Any assessment of that route would require separate neuroengineering evidence.

current_state.text: Yao-Ting Huang, Jake Honma, Omar Hernandez, and colleagues’ “The N2D Haptic Glove: A Multi-Finger Glove for 2D Directional Force Feedback for Contact Rich Manipulation,” dated 12 June 2026, is a preprint reporting benchtop validation and a 16-participant teleoperated scale-pressing study. It documents a relevant advance in directional force feedback. Its experiment does not establish general realism for shape, texture, compliance, slip, or varied two-handed manipulation.

The glove actuates three fingers and provides planar force feedback. It weighs 562 grams excluding its off-hand battery, and the authors identify fatigue during extended use as a limitation. Finger adduction and abduction are outside the reflected force direction. These details matter because the proposed innovation requires useful directional coverage and sustained usability as well as successful force rendering in a restricted task.

The teleoperation results show a bounded advantage. At the 100 g axial target, 2D feedback significantly improved force regulation relative to both visual-only and 1D feedback. The advantage over 1D feedback was not statistically significant at the 50 g axial target or in transverse probing. The result supports useful directional feedback under particular experimental conditions; it does not establish a uniform benefit across the tested conditions or demonstrate the full proposed interface.

The evidence available for this record consists of one paper and the supplied review of it. It cannot establish whether any other system achieves the proposed combination of range, fidelity, and freedom of movement. No bounded search record was supplied, so field-wide coverage through 1 November 2026 remains unresolved. That coverage limitation does not undermine the documented June 2026 findings or establish that the broader capability is impossible.

Access and interpretation limits: the supplied review reports access to the complete retained paper text and references, but the figures themselves were not inspected and some equations had conversion artifacts. The device specifications, study scope, statistical distinctions, and limitations summarized here come from the textual findings described in that review. This record does not add independent inspection or visual verification.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: evaluate varied two-handed tasks involving unfamiliar shapes, incipient slip, textures, and compliant materials. Compare task performance and perceived properties with both physical objects and existing haptic systems. Use blinded comparisons where feasible, and specify which conditions can actually be concealed from participants and evaluators. Success should involve multiple kinds of manipulation; a single force-rendering exercise would establish only that narrower capability.
completion_criteria.label: Varied two-handed manipulation benchmarked against physical objects and haptic systems

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility criteria: define task coverage, participant characteristics, fitting and calibration procedures, comparison conditions, outcome measures, and quantitative acceptance thresholds before evaluation. Report results by task and condition so that average improvements do not conceal important failures. Independent replication, including unfamiliar objects and users, would strengthen the case for generality. These are proposed evaluation requirements, not established consensus standards.
completion_criteria.label: Predefined acceptance thresholds and results by task and condition

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical criteria: demonstrate sustained comfort, movement freedom, and safe failure behavior across users and intended settings. Specify exposure durations, safety limits, and the operating envelope within which the interface delivers reliable feedback. Evaluate how calibration and fitting affect performance and usability. The documented N2D fatigue and calibration concerns motivate these tests, but the paper does not prescribe the proposed protocol or its acceptance thresholds.
completion_criteria.label: Sustained comfort, movement freedom, and safe failure across users

completion_criteria.text: Proposed interpretation boundary: successful finite tests would establish demonstrated breadth within the tested tasks, users, and operating conditions, not literal universality or perfect equivalence to physical objects. Specialized remote applications would still need their own end-to-end validation. Thermal sensation and pain need not be demonstrated to satisfy the scope defined here.
completion_criteria.label: Claims limited to tested tasks, users, and operating conditions

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: HCI-01, “A predictive science of human–computer interaction,” could provide models for predicting haptic perception, learning, and task performance. HCI-03 concerns the resulting interaction capability and hardware; it could advance even while predictive theory remains incomplete.

Roster-based synthesis: HCI-02, “Reliable communication and computer control after profound paralysis,” overlaps if artificial touch is incorporated into neural control systems. Its central outcome is communication and control after paralysis, whereas HCI-03 concerns tactile and force interaction. HCI-04, “An interface that makes inaccessible software operable through a user’s chosen modality,” overlaps when touch becomes an accessible input or output channel. Accessibility through a chosen modality does not itself require realistic physical feedback, and a high-fidelity haptic device would not automatically be accessible to every user.

Roster-based synthesis: HCI-07, “Everyday visual computing with perceptually convincing spatial displays,” is complementary because spatial images and haptic feedback could describe the same digital object. Convincing visual depth does not establish convincing touch. HCI-11, “Remote collaboration with usable shared social and spatial cues,” could incorporate shared haptic manipulation, but its collaboration outcome also depends on coordination and social cues beyond physical feedback.

Roster-based synthesis: HCI-05, “End-user programming that ordinary users can understand and maintain,” could help users author haptic interactions. HCI-06, “Delegation interfaces that keep people in meaningful control of computer work,” could use physical feedback during supervised remote manipulation. Their core breakthroughs concern understandable programming and meaningful control, respectively; neither is established by producing realistic forces or sensations.

Roster-based synthesis: HCI-08, “Real-time conversational interfaces across signed and spoken languages,” HCI-09, “Privacy controls that remain understandable and enforceable across services,” and HCI-10, “Lifelong personal memory augmentation with controllable evidence,” have more indirect relationships. Haptic cues might serve as an additional output channel, while sensing and recording hand interactions could create privacy or memory-design questions. These possible integrations do not make language translation, enforceable privacy, or evidence-controlled memory part of HCI-03’s completion criteria.

change_log.change: Replaced the categorical claim that existing haptic devices lack the proposed combined capability with a bounded account of what the supplied evidence establishes.
change_log.reason: One paper and its related-work discussion cannot determine the state of the entire field, particularly without a supplied bounded search record.

change_log.change: Integrated the 16-participant study, benchtop validation, 100 g and 50 g axial results, and transverse-probing qualification.
change_log.reason: These details preserve the demonstrated advance while preventing a task-specific statistical benefit from becoming a claim of general superiority.

change_log.change: Retained the preprint date, three-finger design, 562 g mass excluding the off-hand battery, and fatigue limitation; added planar coverage, the unreflected direction, and calibration concerns.
change_log.reason: These verified details explain the practical and directional limitations relevant to the proposed breakthrough.

change_log.change: Separated tactile sensation, kinesthetic resistance, directional coverage, perceptual fidelity, and wearable usability within the concept and barriers.
change_log.reason: The review identifies complementary capabilities whose integration matters; force feedback alone does not establish realistic touch.

change_log.change: Preserved direct nervous-system stimulation as an optional route while removing unsupported characterization of its unresolved mechanisms.
change_log.reason: The supplied evidence does not assess neural stimulation, and the concept does not require it.

change_log.change: Expanded the conditional impact account while distinguishing direct interaction benefits from specialized downstream applications.
change_log.reason: Remote surgery, manufacturing, and repair require additional systems and application validation beyond a haptic interface.

change_log.change: Developed the completion proposal with feasible blinding, predefined measures, independent replication, operating boundaries, and limits on generality.
change_log.reason: The original demonstration needed concrete evaluation dimensions without presenting proposed thresholds as consensus standards or finite tests as proof of universality.

change_log.change: Preserved the review’s access and extraction limitations and added explicit roster-based relationships.
change_log.reason: Readers need to understand the evidence boundary and conceptual overlaps without inferring fresh document inspection or merging distinct innovations.

unresolved_issues: Whether any system achieves the proposed combined range, fidelity, and freedom of movement remains unresolved; no bounded field-wide search record was supplied.
The N2D findings remain preprint results. Independent replication or subsequent validation is not established by the supplied inputs.
A completion protocol still needs feasible blinding procedures, task coverage, exposure durations, safety limits, quantitative acceptance thresholds, and a defined practical operating envelope.
The mechanisms, maturity, and limitations of direct nervous-system stimulation require separate evidence if that optional route is developed.
Figures were not inspected in the supplied review, and some equations had conversion artifacts; conclusions requiring those materials remain outside this record’s verified scope.
